newsitem.title: USA: WSCC Board okays 7,200 MW Pacific Intertie rating.
newsitem.headline: WSCC Board okays 7,200 MW Pacific Intertie rating.

text.p: The board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) approved a plan to increase capacity limits on the Pacific Intertie to 7,200 megawatts (MW) from the current rate of 6,250 MW, the reliability council said Friday.
The proposal will still need to be reviewed by the full membership of the WSCC, which has 10 days to do so.
The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) had requested increasing the rating to 7,700 MW, but a compromise was accepted amid concerns raised by some utilities.
The Intertie, which links the Pacific Northwest to Southern California, has a rated capacity of 7,900 MW, but was cut to 5,200 MW after two power blackouts hit the West last summer.
In late March, the WSCC approved increasing the line's capacity to 6,250 MW through the end of June.
